    Wind

    wind.Rmd

    Where did the pollution come from? An animated wind-particle overlay answers that at a glance: streaks flow with the wind, coloured by speed, and advance with the time slider. One parameter adds it:

    library(quickmap)                          # load the quickmap library
heathrow <- from_worldmet(station = "037720-99999", # Heathrow station id
                          year = 2024)              # fetches from NOAA
quickmap(
  from_rdata("episode_london.RData", "pm25", name = "Sensors"),
  boroughs     = c("Wandsworth", "Richmond"),
  colour_scale = "stripes_pm25",
  autoplay     = TRUE,
  play_speed   = 500,
  wind         = heathrow                  # the wind overlay
)

    1. Where the wind data comes from

    from_worldmet() downloads hourly weather-station records from NOAA’s worldwide archive (via the worldmet package — install it and be online for the fetch). Find a station near your map:

    worldmet::getMeta(lat = 51.47, lon = -0.45) # stations near Heathrow,
                                            # with their ids

    For a city-scale map, one representative station is enough — the overlay shows the period-average wind for each time step.

    2. Bring your own wind data

    Any data frame with date, ws (wind speed) and wd (wind direction) columns works — from your own met station, a model, or a file:

    my_wind <- data.frame(
  date = as.POSIXct("2024-01-15 12:00", tz = "UTC") + 3600 * 0:23,
  ws   = 5,                                # m/s
  wd   = 225                               # degrees (from the south-west)
)
quickmap(
  from_rdata("episode_london.RData", "pm25", name = "Sensors"),
  boroughs = c("Wandsworth", "Richmond"),
  wind     = my_wind
)

    Wind hours are matched to the map’s time steps automatically (period means for monthly or annual maps); steps with no wind data show no particles rather than stale ones.

    3. Styling the particles

    The theme’s wind: section controls the look (Styling and themes):

    wind:
  colour_ramp: ["#4575b4", "#74add1", "#8fc3a7",   # blue -> red with speed
                "#fdae61", "#f46d43", "#d73027"]
  particle_density: 0.0033
  line_width: 1.5
  velocity_scale: 0.01

    The default ramp colours particles by wind speed, starting at a visible mid-blue so calm periods still read. On very busy backgrounds a darker single-colour ramp or a heavier line_width stands out more.

    4. Limits worth knowing

    • Interactive maps only — a particle animation has no meaning in a static JPG, so exports omit it.
    • The overlay is a uniform city-scale field from one station; multi-station and gridded (ERA5) wind fields are on the post-1.0 roadmap.
    • A background browser tab may pause the particles until it is foregrounded (a browser behaviour, not a defect).
